chapter: Will Vodery and the road shows
title: Vodery pocketing the band's money and writing parts without a score
summary: Whaley recalls Vodery taking performance money to Paris, finishing a bandmaster exam in twenty minutes and writing parts on the spot, and his Baltimore and Penn background.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Vodery, he was terrific. But he was no good -- I mean, no good that way. He'd get -- we'd go out and play for the lieutenant, go in the lieutenant's office, the captain's bungalow and we'd play. And they'd give us money, we never saw any money. Vodery would take the money and go on to Paris and ball.
Well, wasn't that the usual procedure?
Yeah, they used to do it. And --
But what kind of musician was he?
Oh, he was great. He did a concert out in France there, he did a concert which the bandmasters had a -- what do you call it?
Reproduction? Reproduction of it?
You'd have to take a -- what do you call it, go to school, like.
Oh, take a course.
Take a course, yeah. And it would take the majority of them two hours to do, he'd do it in 20 minutes.
The examination, yeah.
Examination, yeah. Well, anyway, the man says, hey, you ain't finished. He said, man, it's all finished. He did in 20 minutes what it took the average person two hours to do.
He's the one that could write in score ink because he knew he was right.

He'd tell everybody, give me some manuscript papers, stand out in front of the band, and all that noise going on. And he'd write and throw a part to each one, and then says, ten dollars for every bad note. There was no bad note. He was the first man I ever seen do that.
He was the only person I ever saw do it,

too. And it's amazing, this is a black man and our young black children and young American children don't know about these kind of beautiful -- do you know where he was really from? He's gone now. Do you know what part of the country he grew up?
Baltimore. He went to Penn University.
Yeah, he graduated Penn College.
Penn University.
Yeah.
Well, I'm sure the records would be up there.
Yeah.
I must look that up.
